Give an AI that can browse your product page and it lists every checkout obstacle an agent would hit.

OpenAI launched ChatGPT Wallet on 13 November, so its agents can now pay on a merchant's own checkout. A CAPTCHA, a forced account or a bot challenge can stop that purchase, and it may not show up in anyone's report.

In this clip Hannah and I go through two jobs to hand to AI. The first is the checkout walk above. For the second, give it OpenAI's agent access guide and the name of your security provider. It drafts a short note asking your security team whether verified ChatGPT visits are blocked.

The podcast voices are AI-generated.

The full episode and article are at https://manual-focus.co.uk/blog/chatgpt-wallet-agent-checkout-ecommerce/
clips.text: Get AI on this. Walk your own checkout the way an agent would and list every obstacle. Give it your checkout URLs from product page to payment, and an AI that can browse. It hands back each step with every CAPTCHA, forced sign-up and pop-up it hit, and marks the ones it couldn't get past. Get AI on this, too. Write the note to your security team. Give it OpenAI's agent access guide and the name of your security provider, and it drafts a short request asking whether OpenAI's verified cloud browser visits are blocked, with the exact rule to check for that provider.

clips.linkedin:
ChatGPT Wallet needs no integration, so the work moves to whoever runs your bot rules.

OpenAI launched Wallet on 13 November. Its agents use your normal checkout, and you still own orders, fulfilment, customer support and fraud decisions.

In this clip Hannah and I talk about what that means in practice. OpenAI's own guide says its cloud browser can trigger bot detection and cause purchases to fail, so a CAPTCHA, a forced account or a bot challenge from your CDN now sits between the agent and the order.

Worth one question to your security team this week.

The podcast voices are AI-generated.

The full episode and article are at https://manual-focus.co.uk/blog/chatgpt-wallet-agent-checkout-ecommerce/
clips.text: So the merchant doesn't build anything. No Wallet-specific integration at all, OpenAI says. The merchant gets a network token instead of the full card number, plus a reference that links it to the customer's account. And the merchant still owns orders, fulfilment, customer support and fraud decisions. That's the part I'd underline for an ecommerce team. No integration sounds like no work, but it really means the work has moved somewhere else. It's moved into security. OpenAI's own guide says the cloud browser can trigger bot-detection systems and cause purchases to fail. So the CAPTCHA, the forced account, the bot challenge from your content delivery network, all of that now sits between the agent and the order.
